scholarly_anchors: King, K. L. (2003). The Gospel of Mary of Magdala: Jesus and the First Woman Apostle. Polebridge Press.
Pasquier, A. (1983). L'Evangile selon Marie (BG 1). Laval University Press.
Tuckett, C. M. (2007). The Gospel of Mary. Oxford University Press.
encoding_notes: The Gospel of Mary describes the soul's ascent through seven hostile Powers (psychological gatekeepers), making it structurally unique as the only bottom-up cosmology in the corpus. However, for DAG protocol consistency (direction-agnostic approach), we encode the hierarchy top-down: Silence/Rest as source, descending through the Powers to Material World. The topology is identical whether read top-down or bottom-up — a deep linear chain (depth 8). This is the deepest linear chain in the corpus alongside Sethian (depth 7) and Proclean (depth 7). Critically, this tradition has no Sophia fall, no Demiurge, no Aeons, and no Pleroma — it is entirely psychological/experiential, not cosmogonic.

nodes.name: Silence / Rest (Anapausis)
nodes.description: The ultimate state — Silence and Rest beyond all the Powers. The soul's destination after overcoming all seven gatekeepers. In the direction-agnostic encoding, this is the source/apex of the hierarchy.

nodes.name: Power 7: Wrathful Wisdom
nodes.description: The seventh and final Power — Wrathful Wisdom. It has seven forms: Darkness, Desire, Ignorance, Zeal for Death, Kingdom of Flesh, Foolish Wisdom, and Wisdom of the Wrathful.

nodes.name: Power 6: Foolish Wisdom
nodes.description: The sixth Power. A form of wisdom that is foolish — knowledge without gnosis, understanding without liberation.

nodes.name: Power 5: Kingdom of Flesh
nodes.description: The fifth Power — the dominion of bodily existence. Not the body itself but the soul's identification with and subjection to bodily existence.

nodes.name: Power 4: Zeal for Death
nodes.description: The fourth Power — the compulsive drive toward death and destruction. The soul's attachment to mortality and fear.
nodes.encoding_note: Lacuna in text — some reconstruction from P.Oxy. 3525

nodes.name: Power 3: Ignorance
nodes.description: The third Power — Ignorance. Not mere lack of knowledge but active not-knowing, the soul's forgetting of its true nature. The inverse of Gnosis.

nodes.name: Power 2: Desire (Epithumia)
nodes.description: The second Power — Desire/Craving. The soul's attachment to material existence and sensory experience.

nodes.name: Power 1: Darkness (Skotos)
nodes.description: The first Power — Darkness. The most material, the densest veil over the soul. The starting point of the ascent, the lowest gatekeeper.

nodes.name: Material World / Body
nodes.description: The material world and embodied existence — the starting point of the soul's journey in the text's narrative (ascending), and the terminal node in the DAG encoding (descending from source).

edges.description: Hierarchy descends from Silence/Rest through the Powers
Kingdom of Flesh -> Zeal for Death

direction_sensitive_ascending.description: Reverse the DAG to encode the text's actual direction of travel: Material World as root, ascending through the Powers to Silence/Rest as terminal node. All edges become contraction. Topologically identical (linear chain, depth 8) but semantically inverted.
direction_sensitive_ascending.scholarly_support: King (2003) emphasises the ascent direction as theologically primary — the text is fundamentally about liberation through upward movement, not downward emanation.

edges_modified.description: Soul rises from matter through Darkness
Soul overcomes Ignorance, encounters Zeal for Death
Soul overcomes Zeal, encounters Kingdom of Flesh
Soul overcomes Flesh, encounters Foolish Wisdom
Soul overcomes Foolish Wisdom, encounters Wrathful Wisdom
Soul overcomes final Power, arrives at Silence/Rest

direction_sensitive_ascending.encoding_note: HIGH — topologically identical, will be run as supplementary direction-sensitive analysis
